title: innovin — Calm Home (Stoic · Sweatcoin · Ro · Ahead)

Decision.dc.html.title: Why not Duolingo, and what instead

brief.text:
THE BRIEF — what Home must do (same for all four)

Who: 45 people, hybrid, 8 office days a month is mandatory, mostly Android, PWA.

1. Check in at the door. People do it standing, one-handed, so the action is docked in the thumb zone above the tab bar, not at the top of a 6.5" screen. Location is checked BEFORE the tap and shown as a chip, so the tap never fails.

2. "Will I make 8?" Show pace, not just a count: done + planned against 8, with a plain verdict (Done / On track / Plan X more). Planned days look different from done days. Try Remote in Play: today drops out of the plan and the spare day disappears.

3. Home is today, in time order. Before check-in, check-in is the hero. After it, the hero shrinks to one confirmation line and the next thing (tea round, closes 10:45) moves up.

4. Who's around answers "who will I see". Your usual crowd (people who share your days) by face and status first; the office total second.

5. Feed on Home shows only what needs you (RSVP, poll). Passive posts stay in Feed, so there is no duplicate entry point.

6. Steps and reading are opt-in hobbies: smallest, last.

Wi-Fi check lives in Account (nav decision of 10 Nov), so it is off the header.

whyA.text:
A · STOIC — why each piece

• "where are you today?" Stoic asks one question at a time. Check-in is a question, not a form, and the soft lowercase voice takes the edge off a mandatory rule.
• Week strip: Stoic uses it for journal days; for us it IS the office calendar. Filled = done, ring = planned, so the week's plan reads at a glance. Weekdays only, because the office is shut at weekends.
• One centred card, one decision. The pace card says the verdict first ("on track.") and the numbers second.
• The black pill appears once per state, for the one primary action. Everything else is a text link, so actions never compete.
• Name chips for your usual crowd: you are looking for people, so names, not a number.
• Letter-spaced labels instead of card chrome keep the grey page quiet.

whyB.text:
B · SWEATCOIN — why each piece

• The ring is Sweatcoin's one big number. Ours is cut into 8 segments because the rule is 8 separate days: solid = done, outlined = planned, faint = still needed. You see the gap without reading.
• Deep indigo instead of bright violet keeps Sweatcoin's focused "night stadium" feel but drops the arcade look the team objected to.
• Big round check-in button under the ring: Sweatcoin's boost button already sits where the thumb is, and ours is the one daily action.
• Leaderboard rows only where ranking is real: the step league. Who's around is a face strip, never a ranking; ranking colleagues by attendance would feel like surveillance.
• Today's extras (tea, potluck) are swipe cards so the hero stays above the fold.

whyC.text:
C · RO — why each piece

• Ro is a care app: it states your status plainly and tells you what happens next. Office days are a policy, so that clarity fits better than play.
• Big light headline plus one sentence ("You're on track: 5 done, 4 planned") gives the answer before the detail.
• Today timeline is Ro's "What's next". Our day really is time-ordered (check in, tea 10:45, potluck Thu), so a timeline is its true shape.
• Green status tag after check-in: Ro uses tags for confirmed states, and it is proof the check-in worked.
• Grey rows with chevrons are places to go (steps, reading, poll); flat text is information.
• Navy people card: Ro's care-team card shows the humans behind the service. Ours shows your usual crowd.

whyD.text:
D · AHEAD — why each piece

• Ahead's "Technique of the day" becomes "Right now": exactly one thing, picked by time of day (check in, then tea, then potluck). The gradient is used only on that card, so colour means "act now".
• The ring motif in that card doubles as a location radius, the "you're at the office" signal.
• Ahead's dotted skill track becomes 8 office-day stops: filled = done, ringed = planned, open = needed.
• Outlined stat trio (Ahead's activities / streak / time) becomes who's in (your crowd's faces), steps and reading: a status row that is information, so it's outlined, not filled. Office days aren't repeated there because the track above already shows them.
• Docked violet button: Ahead puts its one main action full-width at the bottom; that's also where the thumb is at the door. The gradient card above explains it, and after check-in the card turns into the tea round, then the potluck.
• Figtree is innovin's own brand font and has the same friendly geometric feel as Ahead's type.
• Ahead's mascot is left out on purpose: the team reads mascots as childish.

exploreVerdict.text: Verdict after research (see the Recommendation page): B (Sweatcoin) and D (Ahead) are motivation apps. Their rings, gradients and leagues put a game on top of a mandatory rule, which is the same mistake as Duolingo. A (Stoic) and C (Ro) are calm and trustworthy, but they are built for one person alone, so they are weak at the social side: who's in, kudos, events.

m3title.text: Recommendation: Material 3, with Strava and Mozi patterns

whyHome.text:
HOME — why each component

• Extended FAB "Check in": Material puts a screen's single main action in a FAB at the bottom right, where the thumb is at the door. Android users already know it. It disappears after check-in, so it never nags.
• Location assist chip shows "At the office · 40 m" before you tap, so the tap never fails. Remote is a tonal button, not hidden: being remote is legitimate, not a failure.
• Office days as real dates, not a score. Strava's month view circles actual days; we circle this month's office dates (filled = done, outlined = planned). A plain verdict line ("On track, 1 spare day") is informational feedback, not a streak to lose.
• Who's around as a carousel of people (Mozi's pattern): face, name, and when they're in. It answers "who will I see".
• Tea round card appears only after check-in, with a filled button and a text button: one decision, time-boxed.
• "Needs you" uses M3 list items: the RSVP button sits inline, and a poll row has a chevron.
• Steps and reading sit under "Your extras", opt-in, with a Strava-style privacy line.
• Navigation bar: the standard Android 5-tab bar with a pill indicator and a badge on Feed.

whyDays.text:
DAYS — why each component

• Month grid (Strava's progress calendar): done days filled, planned days outlined, leave marked L, weekends greyed. You see the whole month's plan without arithmetic.
• The verdict card is at the top because "will I make 8?" is the reason to open this page. It is informational, never "you're failing".
• "Still to plan" (revised 17 Nov) plans from your own target, not from who else is in: "2 more office days needed in November. These weekdays are still open." It lists up to 4 open weekdays with Add, and no names, faces or crowd reasons. When you're on track it says so and offers a spare day.
• Tapping "Add" plans the day and the verdict updates at once (try it in Play).
• Leave goes to Zoho People (decision of 9 Nov); here it's just a tonal button with a note on who approves.
• Coming up lists your planned days with a plain note ("Your usual day" or "Added by you"). No faces or who-else-is-in nudges: the app is for employee welfare, so it never steers you towards days by colleagues (owner ruling, 17 Nov).

whyFeed.text:
FEED — why each component

• Filter chips (M3 filter chips) for the post types: people come for one thing (the event, the poll), so one tap narrows the list. The Notes filter shows the empty state.
• Pinned announcement uses an outline in the brand colour, not a loud banner: it's official, but the same shape as every other post.
• Event, poll and kudos act inline (I'm in, vote, appreciate), so there's no detail page to open. No comments, by decision: Slack already does chat.
• One reaction, "Appreciate", not an emoji picker. Strava has run on a single "kudos" reaction for years: it keeps the feed calm and there's no pressure over which emoji to pick. A face stack shows who appreciated it.
• Poll results stay hidden until you vote, so the early votes don't sway everyone else.
• Kudos shows person → person with no points, which matches the scope decision (no tokens or rewards).
• Photos are real team photos. That is the warmth a cartoon was trying to fake.
• "New post" is a tonal extended FAB: it's secondary here, so it isn't the same strong blue as Check in.

mascotNote.text:
LAPPY — test it under strict rules

What the evidence says: a humanlike character raises "social presence" but not trust. Trust follows competence. Clippy failed because it interrupted and talked down to people, not because it was a character.

So, if Lappy stays:
• Lappy only signs SYSTEM posts (birthdays, anniversaries, the Friday recap) so automated posts don't pretend to be a person.
• Lappy fills empty states.
• Never on attendance, leave, office days or reminders. A mascot nudging you about a mandatory rule is Duo's guilt trip again.
• Never pops up or interrupts, and never sends push notifications.
• It's always on (no toggle, as decided on 17 Nov).

Compare the two Feed boards: the birthday post and the Notes filter are the only differences.

retention.text:
DOES A DIFFERENT, NON-AI-LOOKING UI IMPROVE RETENTION?

Partly. Looking distinctive helps the first impression, which forms in about 50 ms and colours later judgements of usability (Lindgaard 2006). But:

1. Unfamiliar layouts are judged LESS attractive. Google's study found people prefer simple and prototypical designs (Tuch et al. 2012).
2. People spend most of their time in other apps, so they expect ours to work the same way (Jakob's law).
3. Novelty wears off within weeks. Return visits come from a habit loop (cue, routine, reward) and from real value.
4. Check-in is mandatory, so people open the app anyway. The voluntary parts (feed, kudos, steps) live or die on whether colleagues post, which is a content problem, not a styling one.
5. A custom system costs a small dev team maintenance and accessibility work that Material components already cover.

So be different where it's cheap and true (real photos, real names, innovin's colour, voice and copy, a few signature moments) and familiar where it costs (navigation, controls, structure).

What "AI-generated" actually looks like: gradient washes, emoji icons, stat-card grids, filler copy. Real content is what avoids it, not an odd layout.

whyCatchup.text:
FEED, CATCH-UP STACK — why each component

• Only posts that are NEW since your last visit go in the stack, so it's finite (5 here). It ends with "You're all caught up", Instagram's 2018 stopping point.
• Swipe right = Seen, left = Later. This is Slack's Catch up mapping. It never means "no" to a colleague: swipe UIs invite snap judgements (CHI 2022), so swiping only sorts your attention.
• Visible Later / Undo / Seen buttons and a hint line: hidden gestures get missed (NN/g), and WCAG 2.5.1 requires a tap alternative.
• Actions stay inside the card (I'm in, vote, appreciate, wish), so swiping is never the way you answer.
• Progress bars on top show how much is left, so it feels finishable.
• "Review later" brings back what you skipped.
• The "Earlier" list is always under the stack: carousel data says content past the first card is rarely seen, so nothing lives only in the stack.
• Lappy signs the birthday card, following the system-post rule.

protoHow.text:
HOW TO USE — press Play, then tap around. State carries across screens:

• Home: tap Check in or Working remote in the "Not checked in yet" card. Location is checked once. To see the "too far" and "location off" states, set Tweaks › Demo › location to far or denied.
• Tea round appears on Home and Snacks only after you check in. Say yes and Lappy shows up with a cup. To see "Tea's on its way", turn on Tweaks › Demo › teaClosed. Skip gets no Lappy.
• Feed is Stories-style: swipe left for the next post, right to go back (or use ‹ ›). Anything you don't answer (the potluck RSVP, the poll) shows under "Still open" until it closes.
• The important announcement (office closed 27 Nov) opens as a sheet on launch. After "Got it", Fri 27 shows as Closed on Days and it's pinned under Feed › Earlier.
• Check in: the card turns green, a check mark draws itself, then it collapses into the status chip. Working remote does the same with a house icon.
• Saying "I'm in" to the potluck on Home also shows as Going in the Feed, and the other way round.
• Days: Add Thu 19 or Tue 24 and the verdict updates.
• Your extras on Home lead to 10K steps (type steps, e.g. 4000, to reach 10K and see Lappy) and Reading ("I finished it").
• The bell opens Notifications, a separate page as decided on 11 Nov.
• Wi-Fi check: the Wi-Fi icon in the Home header (desktop: next to Notifications). Run it, then report a slow result with where you're sitting. Tweaks › Demo › wifiResult switches between slow and good.
• Speak up: the dark icon-only floating button (speech bubble with a shield) on Home, Days, Snacks and Account (desktop: sidebar). Pick a topic, write, and send anonymously; you get a reference and a My reports list.

The phone is 390×844 and each tab scrolls inside it. The reasons for each component are on the "Recommendation: Material 3" page.
• Try: Wave on a crowd card; Nudge in the step league and switch Last 7 days / Today; run the Wi-Fi check and tap the moving packet.
• Days: tap any future date. A sheet offers "Plan to come in" (or "Remove from my plan") and "Apply for leave", with each leave type and what's left, a half-day option for Casual, and "Send request" to Zoho. The day then shows as "Leave requested" (dashed).
• Feed › Post (desktop: New post) opens a sheet: Kudos, Poll, Quote or Feedback. Posting adds it to Earlier.
• Say hi on a crowd card: pick a gesture or invite, choose a time, send. See the incoming invite from Arjun in Notifications.
• Days: "Leave left" chips sit right under the calendar header, so you see your balance while planning. Pending requests count against it.
• Feed: after you're caught up, "Start over" replays the new posts.
• The reading list is out of the design for now.

desktopHow.text:
DESKTOP — why it differs from the phone

• Sidebar instead of a bottom bar, with 10K steps and Reading list promoted to the sidebar, as decided on 10 Nov.
• Check-in is an inline strip at the top, with the same location check as the phone. Laptop location can be rough, so the error suggests checking in from your phone.
• Feed has no swipe stack: a mouse can't swipe, and a wide screen shows all 5 new posts at once. New posts come first, then a "You're all caught up" divider (Instagram's 2018 marker), then Earlier. "Still open" sits in the right rail.
• Home's right rail holds the glanceable things (tea, coming up, steps, reading), and the centre holds what you act on.
• It's a responsive page: it stacks to one column on narrow windows.

catchupRevised.text: Revised on 16 Nov: "Later" is replaced by Back / Next. Unanswered items stay in "Still open" until they close. See Decision §10 and the Prototype page.

importantWhy.text:
IMPORTANT ANNOUNCEMENTS, revised 17 Nov (the owner disliked the banner pushing content down)

• Shown ONCE, as a bottom sheet on phone or a dialog on desktop, the first time you open the app after it's posted. Material reserves dialogs for rare, critical information that needs acknowledging, and admins keep "Important" for closures, policy and safety, so a one-time interruption is justified.
• "Got it" closes it for good. "See in Days" opens the calendar.
• After that it lives where it changes a decision: Fri 27 is marked "Closed" on the Days calendar (dashed grey, can't be planned, with a Closed legend entry), plus a pinned row under Feed › Earlier.
• Home doesn't show it again. Persistent top banners get skipped past and push today's content down. (In the real app, the day before, it could appear once in Up next as "Office closed tomorrow".)
• It isn't in the Stories pager either, where a flick would skip it.
• One push notification when it's posted. The admin sees only a count ("seen by 31 of 45").

speakWifiWhy.text:
SPEAK UP & WI-FI CHECK — placement (owner, 17 Nov)

Both moved out of Account, so each still has only one way in.

• Speak up is a quiet last line on Home (a sidebar item on desktop). It's rare but important, and it only works if people can find it and trust it. The screen leads with what admins can and can't see. It leaves out the time (only the day) so a message can't be matched to who was in at that hour, and points serious issues to [HR CONTACT]. A reference code and a "My reports" list on this device let people see replies without an account trail.
• Wi-Fi check is an icon in the Home header. It runs anywhere, but reporting needs check-in, so reports are about the office Wi-Fi. A report attaches the result and where you're sitting, and tells you if others reported too, so it doesn't feel like shouting into a void.

playWhy.text:
ICONS, PINGS, A MINI-GAME — why, and where not

• Icons with labels on list rows and tiles, like Google Pay does with Material. Icons help people scan, but only with a label, because few icons are universally understood.
• Home extras are tiles with an icon plus a visual (step ring, book progress), not plain text rows.
• Say hi (crowd cards): quick gestures (Wave, High five, Thanks) or invites that lead to meeting in person (Chai break, Lunch, Walk) with a time; the other person replies in one tap from Notifications. Up to 3 a day. Hybrid work shrinks contact with people outside your own team (Microsoft, 61k staff), and brief chats with acquaintances lift mood (Sandstrom & Dunn).
• Nudge (step league): a friendly "time for a walk?", only to people who joined the league, max once a day each.
• Mini-game in the 8-second Wi-Fi check ("catch the packets"). Occupied time feels shorter than empty waiting (Maister 1985), and Chrome's offline dino game is played about 270M times a month, a lot of it in India. It's optional, the test runs either way, and the score shows on the result.
• Leaderboards now show bars relative to the leader, avatars, a 7-day chart with a 10K goal line, and "X steps to pass Kiran": a nearby target motivates more than a rank. Snacks show pick-share bars and the order deadline.
• Still never: games, waves or nudges on attendance, leave or office days.

verdictWhy.text:
VERDICT COLOURS (17 Nov)

• Green = fine: "On track" (even with no spare day, since 8 of 8 planned meets the rule) and "Done for November". Exactly 8 now reads "On track. Every planned day counts", not "Tight".
• Amber only when you must act: "Plan 2 more".
• Not blue: blue is the app's colour for buttons and links, so a blue status would look tappable.
• No red: this is a mandate, and red would read as a warning.
• Every state has a text label, so colour is never the only signal.
• Calendar: today has a dark ring plus a "Today" legend entry, and its screen-reader label says "today". "11 weekdays left in November, including today" replaces "11 working days left".

metricsRule.text:
NUMBERS RULE (17 Nov): show a number only if it changes what you do, or answers a question you'd actually ask.

Removed:
• "5 done · 3 planned · 8 needed": the verdict and the dates already say it.
• "11 weekdays left": now only shown when you're short of days.
• "14 in the office": your crowd's faces answer the real question.
• Tea headcounts (9 said yes, 10 people this round): you drink tea or you don't.
• "12 appreciated", "21 wished her": public counts on kudos and birthdays invite comparison in a 45-person team. You see your own action instead.
• "X people picked" (snacks) and "day 6 of 8" (a repeat).

Kept, and why:
• Potluck "18 going": helps decide whether, and how much, to bring.
• Poll % after voting: the result is the point.
• Per-snack picks: tells you whether your pick is likely to be ordered.
• Steps, league and "X to pass": the opt-in competition is the point.
• Wi-Fi speeds and "2 others reported": the diagnosis, and proof it's known.
• Suggestion +counts: they decide what gets promoted.
• "Quiet day: 9 planned": helps you pick a day.
• Badges and the 2/5 counter: they tell you what's left to do.

homeLayout.text:
HOME LAYOUT (17 Nov), after the owner said it read as a plain stack of boxes

• One focal point: "Up next" is a time-ordered list (tea 11:00, potluck Thu, poll closes Thu) with a time column, so you scan by when, not by box.
• Once you've checked in, the big confirmation card collapses into a chip under the greeting ("In office · since 9:12 · Change"). A finished task shouldn't keep prime space.
• Office days shows a fixed Mon–Fri "This week" strip with the verdict beside it, so nothing wraps; the full month lives in Days.
• One surface: white cards on a grey ground, with colour kept for meaning (status chip, verdict) instead of a different tint per card.
• The tea text repeated the time ("Closes 10:45" and "Answer by 10:45"); now it's said once.

plainAudit.text:
PLAINNESS AUDIT (17 Nov)

Rule: glanceable and social screens get structure and visuals; settings, forms and trust screens stay plain on purpose, because there familiarity beats flair.

Changed:
• Status chip on one line: "In office · 9:12", with Change as its own link.
• Invite time: a –/+ stepper in 15-minute steps instead of the native time field.
• Desktop Home now matches the phone: status chip, time-ordered Up next (tea folded in), and a Mon–Fri week strip; the rail keeps Coming up, steps and reading.
• Days (phone): Coming up is now swipeable day tiles (no faces since 17 Nov: no who-else-is-in nudges).
• Notifications: an icon per type (tea, event, leave, kudos).
• Reading: team-shelf rows show book spines.
• Leave card: icon.

Kept plain on purpose: Account (settings), Speak up (anonymity needs a calm, form-like screen), Wi-Fi report, and the New post composer.

heroes.text:
ILLUSTRATED PAGE HEADERS (17 Nov), after Google Pay

• Only on the pages the bottom nav or sidebar leads to: Home, Feed, Days, Tea & snacks and Account, plus 10K steps and Reading list on desktop. Detail screens (Wi-Fi, Speak up, Notifications) stay plain.
• Each page gets its own tint and a flat scene: Home is Lappy at different times of day; Feed a pinboard; Days a calendar and a path to a flag; Tea & snacks a cup and a plate; Account hills behind your profile (like Google Pay's profile); Steps footprints on a path; Reading a bookshelf.
• Flat and muted, with no characters, so it reads as Google Pay and not as Duolingo.
• The title sits left, at most ~60% wide, and the art sits right, so text never sits on the illustration.
• These are drawn placeholders; real illustrations would come from a designer in the same style.

Time of day (17 Nov): the Home header changes with the time. Morning: soft blue, sun low. Afternoon: bright sky, sun high, more clouds. Evening: dusk indigo, moon, stars, lit windows and light text. The greeting changes to match. Preview it with Tweaks › Demo › timeOfDay (morning / afternoon / evening / auto).
Owner's call (17 Nov): Lappy replaces the Google Pay-style building on Home. Morning: Lappy with chai. Afternoon: waving. Evening: dozing under the moon. Same flat, muted style, no speech bubbles or messages, so the character sets the mood but never nags. No innovin logo in the art (it needs stakeholder approval).

remoteRule.text:
STATUS-AWARE CONTENT (17 Nov)

Rule: before check-in, show everything, because it helps you decide whether to go in. Once you've marked Remote, hide what only matters in the office today, and swap in what helps you plan.
• Home: "In office today" (names kept) becomes "12 planned in on Wed 18" with a Days link: a count only, no faces, so it doesn't steer you by who's in. The tea round never shows (it's office-only).
• Snacks: today's pick list becomes "You're remote today". Suggestions for coming days stay.
• Notifications: the tea round reminder is hidden.
• Wi-Fi report needs check-in; Feed and Days are unchanged.

Also: the separate "On track" banner on Days is gone. The verdict is a chip on the calendar card, the same as Home, and the "weekdays left" hint shows only when you're short.

Microinteractions: buttons press in when tapped; toggles pop when switched on (RSVP, vote, appreciate, plan a day, snack pick, Say hi); progress and leaderboard bars animate; the nav highlight fades; check-in has its success animation. All of it switches off under reduced motion.

Feed cards: tinted by post type, with a soft corner circle in the type's colour, instead of plain white.

noGroupism.text: Owner ruling, 17 Nov: the app is for employee welfare. No suggestions based on who else is in. Days plans from your own target ('Still to plan'); Home's 'In office today' keeps names; the remote card shows a count only.

adminApp.text: Admin app (18 Nov): its own shell, same Material 3 system. Reached from Account → Admin. Leave decisions stay in Zoho; Speak up, snack picks and Wi-Fi reports stay anonymous; birthdays are entered here.
